front.title: The MARS Rating: Machine-Adversary Resistance to Autonomous AI Attack

abstract.t: This document defines MARS (Machine-Adversary Resistance), an open rating, from 0 to 5, of how well a defended asset resists an autonomous artificial-intelligence adversary: an attacker that performs reconnaissance, exploitation, adaptation and propagation at machine speed and scale with no human in the loop. MARS is not a control catalogue and not a maturity model. It is a resistance rating, scored on five axes that describe adversary capabilities -- the ability to Learn a surface, Reuse a success, Scale by automation, Outpace a defence, and sPread from a foothold -- plus a requirement for tamper-evident, independently verifiable evidence at the highest levels. Because the axes are defined as adversary capabilities rather than specific technologies, MARS applies to any asset an AI can attack. This document specifies the threat model, the five axes, the rating scale, the assessment tiers, the assessment method, the evidence requirement, and a profile mechanism by which the invariant rubric is interpreted for any deployment substrate.
